summary:
What if a student could experience the journey to space before ever becoming an astronaut?

RocketSim makes that possible.

RocketSim is a virtual reality space simulation game where students don't just study rocket science — they step inside it. They build rockets with their own hands, make real engineering decisions, and experience the thrill of launching into space. Also accessible through a web browser, RocketSim brings this experience to more students.

Every mission is powered by real physics and NASA datasets. Players manage budgets, balance rocket components, and journey toward orbit, space stations, or the Moon. When something fails, they don't simply lose. They discover why, improve their designs, and try again.

Our goal isn't just to teach students how rockets work. It's to make them feel that they could build one.

Because somewhere in a classroom today is a future astronaut, engineer, or scientist who hasn't discovered their potential yet.

RocketSim could be the moment they do.
details:
RocketSim is a web-based virtual reality game that transforms rocket science into a hands-on experience. Instead of simply watching space missions, students become aerospace engineers, building, testing, and launching their own rockets in an immersive 3D environment.

Players choose a mission: reaching Earth's orbit, visiting a space station, or traveling to the Moon. Inside a virtual hangar, they assemble rockets using engines, fuel tanks, crew capsules, solar panels, and antennas. Each component affects the rocket's weight, performance, and cost. An interactive checklist checks launch readiness, while illustrated guides explain the science behind each part. Students then enter the cockpit, launch their rockets, control their flight, and learn from failures by improving their designs.

RocketSim is developed using Vite, TypeScript, Three.js, WebXR, and WebGL, with Cloudflare for hosting. It supports immersive VR gameplay through compatible browsers and is also accessible without a VR headset. Our simulations use real NASA datasets, including planetary measurements, Earth's atmosphere, and astronauts' needs, with calculations tested against NASA's published values.

What makes RocketSim unique is its combination of physical interaction in VR, realistic engineering challenges, and NASA-based science. Our team focused on scientific accuracy, accessibility, realistic budgets, intuitive controls, and learning through experimentation. Instead of memorizing formulas, students see how engineering decisions affect real mission outcomes, developing problem-solving skills, creativity, and interest in STEM.

Our ultimate goal is to make space exploration feel achievable. Because somewhere in a classroom today is a future aerospace engineer who simply hasn't discovered their potential yet. RocketSim could be the experience that changes that.
